packageDirectories.versionDescription: Replay guard. Platform Event delivery is at-least-once, and the framework now treats it that way: every event reaching any of the three subscribers passes through CursorBatchReplayGuard before anything is dispatched or counted. This is the response to a production incident in which the event bus rewound the committed subscriber offset for CursorBatch_Worker__e and re-delivered roughly 51,000 already-acknowledged events, the oldest 103 hours old on a StandardVolume channel documented to retain 24. Nobody re-published anything; in that hour the channel recorded 43 publishes against 51,085 deliveries. Because the worker trigger enqueued a job on every delivery with no idempotency check, the redelivery re-executed real business logic: 314,453 asynchronous jobs in about ninety minutes against a baseline of 10,000-15,000 per day, with destructive downstream writes and customer contact outside permitted calling hours. The guard applies three independent layers, so no single loosened setting leaves a subscriber defenceless. Job state rejects events whose CursorBatch_Job__c is missing, terminal, or already has Completed_At__c, using one non-locking SOQL per subscriber batch. Staleness rejects events older than the new CursorBatch_Config__mdt.Max_Event_Age_Minutes__c (blank uses 60; -1 disables) at no cost, since an event carries its own CreatedDate. Exactly-once inserts a row into the new CursorBatch_Event_Ledger__c keyed on a unique Event_Key__c, where a DUPLICATE_VALUE is proof the event was already processed. Job state is tested before staleness even though staleness is cheaper, because the batch's job query has already run: that ordering makes a STALE verdict mean specifically 'the job is live and this shard arrived late', and it is why a replay of the 2026-08-24 shape resolves entirely to JOB_TERMINAL and produces no follow-on work. Event identity is per channel. Worker events are W#jobRecordId#cursorQueryId#workerNumber - they are published exactly once per worker at fan-out, so the shard is the identity, and including the cursor queryId is load-bearing because a legitimate coordinator retry rebuilds its cursor and must be allowed to fan out again while a redelivery carrying the original queryId collides. Coordinator events are C#jobRecordId#coordinatorClass, the class component keeping CSV_Ready and CSV_Error callbacks from colliding with the initial dispatch. Completion events keep the pre-existing jobRecordId#replayId format so operational queries still read. Keys over 255 characters become a SHA-256 digest. Blocking is never allowed to strand a job. Total_Workers__c still counts a rejected shard, so without reconciliation the job could never reach a terminal status - and because isJobAlreadyRunning treats Processing as running, every future submission of that job name would silently return null, retiring the job permanently on one dropped event. A STALE rejection on the worker channel therefore publishes the same completion event a worker publishes after exhausting its retries, so the shard counts as a failed worker and all terminal-transition, parent-mirror and finish() routing stays in CursorBatchCompletionHandler; on the coordinator channel the job is marked Failed with the reason on Error_Message__c. JOB_TERMINAL, JOB_MISSING and DUPLICATE are deliberately not reconciled. Idempotency now covers every job rather than only those with a state reducer - 7 of 62 configurations in the affected org - and markers are no longer deleted when a job completes, which is exactly why the replay found nothing to collide with. Retention is by age instead, defaulting to 7 days via the new CursorBatch_Settings__c hierarchy custom setting, comfortably past the observed 103-hour horizon. Nothing needs scheduling: CursorBatchCoordinator checks on job submission whether a sweep is due and enqueues CursorBatchLedgerCleanup at most once every 24 hours, using a free getOrgDefaults() read and only out of genuine async slack so it can never consume a caller's queueable slot. CursorBatchLedgerCleanupSchedule is available for orgs preferring a fixed window. The sweep is deliberately not triggered on job completion, because 11,425 jobs went terminal inside 28 minutes during the incident and a completion-triggered sweep would have enqueued 11,425 cleanup jobs on top of the 314,453 already in flight. The completion channel runs on the exactly-once layer alone: a completion event is a report rather than a dispatch, blocking one discards the record that work already happened, and it is the one rejection nothing can reconcile. Rejections are logged once per transaction, aggregated, at ERROR - per-event logging is what pushed the org past its 775,000/hour publish allocation and suppressed all custom platform event publishing org-wide for fifteen minutes, and the org's WARN threshold is what suppressed the INFO lines that would have made diagnosis immediate. Entries carry the 'CursorBatch Replay Blocked' tag and the 'EVENT REPLAY BLOCKED' scope. The ledger write fails open: a non-duplicate DML error admits the event and logs, because the other two layers are still in force and silently dropping legitimate batch work is worse. There is deliberately no switch that turns the guard off. Staleness is the only layer that can reject a legitimate event, because an age threshold is a judgment call, so a job with unpredictable delivery timing narrows exactly that one check with Max_Event_Age_Minutes__c = -1 and keeps the two layers that cannot be wrong by construction. A blanket off switch would surrender the protections with no false-positive risk in order to relax the one that has it, and 'disabled and forgotten' is the state the framework was already in when the replay arrived. Also fixes a latent event-loss defect unrelated to the replay: CursorBatchCompletionHandler incremented Failed_Workers__c without a null guard while the counters around it were guarded, and CursorBatchWorkerCompleteTrigger has no try/catch, so an NPE there would roll back an entire subscriber batch rather than failing one job. CursorBatch_Processed_Event__c and CursorBatchProcessedEventCleanup are deprecated in place and no longer written to or called; existing rows are inert and can be drained then dropped. Nothing was removed from the package.
